answer.rationale: Causal timing points at the release: a build shipped 2h ago and the write-path p99 began climbing ~30min later, single-region. Of the five candidates, only rollback addresses a suspected cause; failover, capacity, breakers, and replica routing all treat symptoms. Two competing hypotheses matter, so I spend the budget on the two memories that would decide between them. I verify memory_b1 because it is the sole basis for 'rollback is safe and effective' and, as consolidated, it is an outcome summary with no record of load conditions — day-18 rollback almost certainly did not occur at settlement peak with heavy in-flight writes, so its 'no customer impact' claim may not transfer. I verify memory_b2 because regional failover is the strongest alternative for a region-confined degradation, and its 'traffic shifted cleanly' likewise omits whether writes were draining under peak; a failover that strands in-flight settlement writes violates the primary objective more severely than continued latency. I am not verifying b3/b4/b5: capacity provisioning was preemptive and cannot be built inside this window, circuit breakers fit a partner dependency failure not an internal write-path regression, and replica routing relieves read pressure on a problem that is write-bound. Note the inherited set is uniformly success stories — six interventions, six wins — which is survivorship bias, not evidence that these levers are low-risk; the failures were never written down. So I do not treat any memory as a green light. I scope to a small guarded test: stage the rollback to a canary slice of write traffic per the gating pattern in memory_b6, confirm p99 recovers on that cohort before widening, and keep write-draining explicit so no settlement writes are lost. If the canary does not recover, the release is exonerated and the next window should investigate a region-local resource fault instead. Downstream risk flagged: a rollback at peak can drop in-flight writes and, if the prior build shares the defect, burns the one available window.
